method: Same selection system as live play: random subjects and formats, then random unseen questions. Recent subjects are avoided to keep the mix varied; first 100.

questions.prompt: Name a character from the Harry Potter books or films.
questions.scope: Identifiable characters in the Harry Potter novels, films and their epilogues count, including creatures, ghosts and portraits. Real actors are not their fictional characters. Same-name characters share one answer identity.

questions.prompt: Name a hotel chain or hotel brand.
questions.scope: Real current or historical hotel, motel, hostel and serviced-apartment brands/chains, branded hotel collections and primarily hotel-operating groups count. Single independent properties, booking/rental marketplaces, private-equity investors and unrelated parent companies do not. Genuine short names and brand renames share an answer.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that can produce its own light.
questions.scope: Bioluminescence, including light produced by symbiotic bacteria in an animal's light organ, counts. Reflection, fluorescence and bright coloring alone do not. Broad animal groups count when they contain documented luminous members.

questions.prompt: Name a piece of camping equipment.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a human muscle or muscle group.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a type of custard or a dessert made with custard.
questions.scope: Named custards and desserts made using custard or custard powder count. A cream-only filling does not qualify merely because it is called cream.

questions.prompt: Name an item that can be used as furnace fuel in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Items actually accepted in the fuel slot count, rather than anything that merely looks flammable. Their fuel value need not be the same. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a record label or record company.
questions.scope: Real current and historical record labels, imprints and record companies count. A publisher, streaming platform or music store is not automatically a record label.

questions.prompt: Name an animation movie.
Name a player who has been on an NFL or AFL roster (1920–2026).
Name a type of toy.
questions.scope: Recognized toy types and established named kinds of plaything count. Named branded toy kinds such as LEGO bricks, Barbie dolls or Play-Doh also count; a company name alone, a fictional character alone or an unrelated household object is not a toy type.

questions.prompt: Name a structure or component found in a living cell.
questions.scope: Plant, animal, fungal and prokaryotic cell structures count. Whole organs or tissues are not structures inside one cell. Established molecular structures such as DNA and chromosomes count. Cellular structures and molecular assemblies count; an individual pigment such as chlorophyll is not an organelle or cell structure by itself.

questions.prompt: Name a tea brand or tea company.
questions.scope: Real current or historical tea brands, tea companies and tea estates count. A tea variety, drink preparation or generic ingredient is not a company or brand. The inventory includes packaged-tea and ready-to-drink brands; owning a separate brand does not automatically make a generic parent-name guess eligible.

questions.prompt: Name a spoken, signed or constructed language.
Name a Legendary or Mythical Pokémon.
questions.scope: Species classified as Legendary or Mythical in the pinned PokéAPI data count. Forms share their species' answer identity. Pseudo-Legendary is a fan label and does not make a species Legendary.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that can deliver venom.
questions.scope: Venom must be injected or delivered by a bite, sting or spine; simply being poisonous is different.

questions.prompt: Name a heist movie.
questions.scope: Films built around a robbery, theft, con or organized caper count, including comedies, animated movies and shorts. Television series, directors and a film with only an unrelated passing theft do not automatically count.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Maroon 5.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Maroon 5 count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer. The same band's earlier releases as Kara's Flowers also count; solo-member features do not.

questions.prompt: Name a cloud type, form or recognized cloud feature.
questions.scope: Cloud genera, species, varieties and recognized cloud features count, along with established common names such as lenticular cloud, contrail and fog at ground level. Weather events, precipitation and a blue sky alone do not count.

questions.prompt: Name an athlete who has played professionally in a team sport.
questions.scope: Men's and women's sports, any country and any era count; no roster-year restriction.

questions.prompt: Name a color or a named shade.
questions.scope: Recognized English color names and published named shades count, including named pigments, Crayola colors and standard CSS color keywords. Regional spellings and ordinary synonyms share one answer. Patterns are not a single color. Different standard definitions of the same ordinary name do not create extra answers.

questions.prompt: Name a cake, torte, or established cake variety.
Name a bird that cannot normally fly, including extinct flightless birds.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a villain from a children's animated TV series.
questions.scope: Named antagonists count even if they sometimes help the heroes.

questions.prompt: Name a landmark people can visit.
questions.scope: Named natural or human-made visitor landmarks count, including ruins.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with k-pop music.
Name a game on Steam tagged “Co-op”.
Name a machine or device that uses an electric motor.
questions.scope: The motor can be internal and does not need to move the entire device.

questions.prompt: Name an exercise that can be done using your bodyweight instead of added weights.
questions.scope: Named exercises and recognized variations count, including floor exercises, holds and movements on a pull-up bar. A bar or bench can provide support; dumbbells and loaded barbells are not required.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of swallow or martin.
questions.scope: Established named groups and species in the Hirundinidae bird family count, including recently extinct species. Common and scientific names are accepted. Real synonyms share an identity; unrelated birds and objects named after birds do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a comedy movie.
Name an item or product used to wash, dry or care for laundry.
questions.scope: Laundry appliances, supplies, stain treatments and clothes-care tools count, as do named product types and established laundry-product brands, including historical ones. A garment itself is not a laundry supply.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish or preparation in which eggs are a main ingredient.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a song with a color in its title.
questions.scope: Ordinary color words in released song titles count; color names used as surnames need context.

questions.prompt: Name a real named cape or headland.
questions.scope: Real named capes, headlands and projecting points of land count, including lake headlands. A city containing the word Cape does not qualify merely because of its name.

questions.prompt: Name an outfit from Fortnite.
questions.scope: Any recorded season or collaboration counts. These are cosmetic names, not Battle Royale weapon names.

questions.prompt: Name a type of tree.
Name a character from Shrek or Puss in Boots.
questions.scope: Named or distinctly identified characters in the Shrek films and spin-offs, including Puss in Boots films, count. Identified groups such as the Three Little Pigs count. Voice actors and generic fairy-tale species alone do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a gas or common gas mixture.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name an item or established style of clothing.
Name a named dish cooked or wrapped in plant leaves.
questions.scope: Traditional leaf-wrapped food parcels, dishes cooked between leaves or in leaf-lined containers, and dishes traditionally sold wrapped in leaves count. Food merely set on a leaf plate without leaf cooking or wrapping does not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has been on the Kansas City Chiefs franchise roster.
questions.scope: Past or present roster membership for this franchise through the retained 2026 snapshot counts, including its earlier names/locations and NFL, AFL or AAFC membership where applicable. Offseason and practice squads count. An unrelated former team sharing the same city or code does not. The current franchise rules and captured seasons are retained for source review.

questions.prompt: Name a named place or map from a video game.
questions.scope: Named maps, towns, regions and locations count; ordinary real-world cities need a named in-game setting.

questions.prompt: Name a stringed musical instrument.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a crime TV or streaming show.
Name a branch or field of mathematics.
questions.scope: Recognized mathematical branches, subfields and established mathematical research disciplines count. Both pure and applied mathematics count. Individual formulas, symbols, isolated theorems and unrelated school subjects do not by themselves name a branch.

questions.prompt: Name a type of flower.
questions.scope: Recognized common flower types and flowering plants grown for their blooms count, including named horticultural groups and documented varieties. Materials merely named after flowers, artificial flower products and unrelated decorative objects do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a type of cookie or biscuit, including named branded varieties.
questions.scope: Named cookie and sweet biscuit varieties, brands and traditional preparations count. Regional names for the same biscuit share one answer; a cake or cracker is not automatically a cookie.

questions.prompt: Name something people can borrow from a public library.
questions.scope: Items must actually be offered by a public library somewhere; Library of Things collections count.

questions.prompt: Name a Pokémon Ability.
questions.scope: Named passive Pokémon Abilities from the core games and Pokémon Conquest count. Moves, types, held items and generic trainer actions are separate concepts.

questions.prompt: Name a category of motor vehicle.
questions.scope: Types of self-propelled road or off-road vehicle count, with wheels, tracks or skids, including electric versions. Individual named models, rail vehicles, unpowered trailers and descriptions of condition alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a type or form of poem.
questions.scope: Recognized named poem and verse forms count, including complete short forms and established stanza/verse forms used as poems. A subject, individual poet, book title or meter alone does not automatically name a poem form.

questions.prompt: Name a musical instrument played by blowing air into it.
questions.scope: Mouth-blown instruments count, including reed, brass and free-reed instruments.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of reptile.
questions.scope: Named reptile groups, species and established kinds count, living or extinct, including non-avian dinosaurs and extinct marine reptiles. Common and scientific names count. Birds and amphibians are outside this ordinary non-avian reptile scope.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has won the NBA regular-season MVP award.
questions.scope: Winners of the main NBA regular-season Most Valuable Player award through the 2025–26 season count. Finals, All-Star and other leagues' MVP awards are different.

questions.prompt: Name a culinary nut or a seed people eat.
questions.scope: Culinary nuts and food seeds count, including grains, pulses, spice seeds and nuts that are not botanical nuts. Traditional foods that require preparation count. A named food seed or nut group counts; a botanical class, tree alone, finished sauce or book title does not.

questions.prompt: Name an object that commonly has a hinge.
questions.scope: A common hinged version of the object must exist. Sliding or roll-up versions do not prevent a genuinely hinged object from counting.

questions.prompt: Name a car, motorcycle, truck or bus manufacturer or brand.
questions.scope: Real current or historical manufacturers and established marques of cars, motorcycles (including racing motorcycles), trucks and buses count, including documented vehicle assembly and coachbuilding firms. A vehicle model alone, a transport operator, an aircraft/rail-only maker, a pure component supplier, a toy or a fictional brand does not count. Actual brand/company names and true renames share an answer.

questions.prompt: Name a video game console or dedicated gaming handheld.
questions.scope: Named released game consoles, dedicated handheld game systems and purpose-built gaming handheld PCs count. Named revisions, early electronic/VHS-based gaming systems and game-library add-on platforms count; regional renames of the same platform share an answer. N-Gage is a documented gaming-handheld hybrid. General-purpose phones/computers, media-streaming boxes with optional games, unreleased prototypes and input-only controllers do not count. A self-contained plug-and-play game unit counts even if its shell resembles a controller.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with rock music.
Name a movie based on a video game.
questions.scope: Released feature films count, including animation; a game based on a movie is the reverse and does not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of animal that can regrow a lost body part.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name one of the 88 official constellations.
questions.scope: Official IAU constellation names count. Recognized common names such as Capricorn and the Great Bear are accepted. Asterisms such as the Big Dipper are only parts of constellations.

questions.prompt: Name an online social or community platform.
questions.scope: Real current or historical general-audience social networks, social media and named online community platforms count, including group communication, public discussion networks and social virtual worlds. Ordinary email, devices, generic internet terms, individual profiles/groups, learning-management software and services dedicated to dating or adult content do not. Actual public names such as X, VK, QQ and Hi5 count; generated initials do not.

questions.prompt: Name a pasta shape.
questions.scope: Named pasta shapes count; sauces and full dishes are separate.

questions.prompt: Name a volcano or named volcanic complex. Dormant and extinct ones count.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a move from a Pokémon video game.
questions.scope: Named moves from released Pokémon games count, including Z-Moves, Max Moves and Colosseum/XD Shadow moves. Physical/special implementations of the same named move share one answer. Generic actions and moves from fan games do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a named vehicle from fiction.
questions.scope: Named fictional vehicles, ships and vehicle models count across film, TV, books, comics and games, including living vehicle characters. Generic words such as car or spaceship, and individual parts that are not vehicles, do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a dance style, traditional dance, or named social dance.
Name a piece of equipment used to take or process photographs.
questions.scope: Physical equipment, supplies and accessories used in still photography count, including darkroom materials. A finished photograph, filmed sequence or a device used only to mark a film take does not.

questions.prompt: Name something you can wear that has a button, zipper or buckle.
questions.scope: Clothes, footwear, accessories and protective wear count.

questions.prompt: Name a water sport or recreational activity on or in water.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a pie, tart or flan.
questions.scope: Named sweet and savory pies, tarts and flans count. Established dishes conventionally called pies count even when they use mash, crumbs or cake, including Boston cream pie and whoopie pie. An ordinary cake without a conventional pie name, pizza or an uncrusted omelette does not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Action”.
Name a type or recognized form of sculpture.
questions.scope: Recognized sculpture forms, sculpting techniques and named sculptural object/material types count. Material words can name an established sculptural type, such as bronze, marble, ice or sand sculpture. Individual artists, individual artworks and generic unrelated objects do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of arachnid.
questions.scope: Named arachnid groups, species and recognized common kinds count. Spiders, scorpions, ticks, mites, harvestmen and other arachnid orders are included. Insects, crustaceans and myriapods are outside this question.

questions.prompt: Name a landlocked country.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a type of lamp or lighting fixture.
questions.scope: Real lamps, lighting fixtures and manufactured light sources count, including candles and historical lighting. Fictional individual lamps, stars and naturally glowing organisms do not.

questions.prompt: Name a type of building.
Name a named pasta or noodle dish.
questions.scope: Named dishes and established menu preparations count, including familiar meal names such as spaghetti, udon and soba, filled pastas and gnocchi. A bare unfilled pasta-shape name without a dish or established menu preparation does not count. Plain tteokbokki is a rice-cake dish; rabokki includes noodles.

questions.prompt: Name a music act known as a duo.
questions.scope: Current and historical musical duos count. Ordinary backing musicians do not change a two-person act into a larger group. Two solo artists who collaborated once are not automatically a named duo.

questions.prompt: Name an emote from Fortnite.
questions.scope: Any recorded season or collaboration counts. These are cosmetic names, not Battle Royale weapon names.

questions.prompt: Name a real animal that has horns or antlers.
questions.scope: Living and extinct animals count, including beetle horns and other actual horn-like structures. Feathers that merely look like horns do not count. A named animal group counts when it contains horned or antlered members.

questions.prompt: Name a driver who has competed in Formula One.
questions.scope: Drivers in the complete Jolpica/Ergast Formula One World Championship driver inventory count, including historical entrants and the Indianapolis 500 when it was part of that championship. A real surname can identify a valid driver; invented initials and racing three-letter codes do not count as names.

questions.prompt: Name a horror movie.
Name a three-dimensional geometric shape.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name a food that is commonly pickled.
questions.scope: Vegetables, fruits, eggs, meats and seafood with established pickled preparations count. Vinegar and brine are ingredients, not foods being pickled.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Linkin Park.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Linkin Park count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer. Released Xero and Hybrid Theory recordings from the same band also count; fan-contest songs do not.

questions.prompt: Name a named weapon from a video game.
questions.scope: Unique named weapons and established weapon/item names count across all platforms.

questions.prompt: Name a hand tool or utensil used to prepare or serve food.
questions.scope: Kitchen hand tools, utensils, serving implements and nonpowered cookware count. Small measuring tools used in food preparation also count. Large powered appliances and foods do not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a plant people eat.
questions.scope: Named edible plants count, including those eaten for fruit, leaves, roots or seeds; fungi are separate.

questions.prompt: Name a fantasy movie.
Name a real castle or palace.
questions.scope: Named castles, palaces and châteaux worldwide count, including historical or ruined ones and real decorative castle attractions. A real theme-park castle based on fiction counts; a castle that exists only in a story and a generic type of building do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish commonly made with chicken.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a scientific discipline or academic field.
questions.scope: Recognized sciences and academic research fields count, including mathematics, social sciences, linguistics, medicine and engineering. Subdisciplines and documented historical names count. A result, isolated technique or pseudoscientific practice is not itself an academic discipline.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with pop music.
Name a player who has played for the Charlotte Hornets.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not. Charlotte Hornets history from 1988–2002 and 2014 onward, and Charlotte Bobcats history from 2004–2014 count. The New Orleans franchise is separate.

questions.prompt: Name an item you can catch by fishing in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Fish, junk and treasure in the ordinary fishing loot tables count. Items merely carried by nearby mobs do not. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a mystery TV or streaming show.
Name a style of coat or jacket.
questions.scope: Named coat and jacket styles count, including workwear and historical garments. Materials alone and coats of paint do not.
